subtitle: Production-Ready Go RabbitMQ Worker Template
description: A minimal, production-ready starting point for Go services that consume messages from RabbitMQ queues, process them, and route outcomes to separate success or failure queues.

techStack.ci: GitHub Actions (build, vet, fmt, test, docker)

architectureHighlights.title: Success/Failure Routing
architectureHighlights.description: Message consumption with automatic success/failure routing built into the handler, based on the outcome of processing.

architectureHighlights.title: Graceful Shutdown
architectureHighlights.description: Listens for SIGINT/SIGTERM and lets in-flight deliveries finish before the process exits.

architectureHighlights.title: Automatic Reconnect
architectureHighlights.description: Connection and retry handling is delegated to wagslane/go-rabbitmq, with a configurable base reconnect delay.

architectureHighlights.title: Message Tracing
architectureHighlights.description: Unique message_id headers and structured logs make individual deliveries traceable end-to-end.

modularInfrastructure.title: cmd/worker
modularInfrastructure.description: Main package handling wiring, config loading, and OS signal handling.

modularInfrastructure.title: internal/rmq
modularInfrastructure.description: Connection setup and the handler responsible for consuming, processing, and routing to success/failure queues.

modularInfrastructure.title: internal/config & internal/model
modularInfrastructure.description: Typed env-var configuration and the message types/envelopes to adapt for a real producer.

setupAndRun.step: Use this template on GitHub, then rename the module
Run with Docker (spins up RabbitMQ too)
Or run locally against your own broker
